Clearly Donnie Yen should be in more games

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The people love a good action RPG. At least that's what the numbers around the launch of Phantom Blade Zero would indicate, since it's managed to shift millions of copies and attract north of 820,000 concurrent players on Steam in its first weekend.

Developer and publisher S-Game shared one of these stats on social media, posting a nice big graphic on Twitter announcing that Phantom Blade Zero crossed the four million mark in copies sold in just three days. An impressive turnaround by any metric.

"Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!" reads the caption. The image notes the Metacritic score of 88 and the Steam review score of 89%. Not too shabby whatsoever.

Phantom Blade Zero has sold over 4 million copies in just 72 hours!🔥 Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support! https://t.co/XPhq14v9YNNovember 2, 2026

Speaking of Valve's store, a healthy amount of these players are jumping into the Phantom World on PC. On Steam Charts, the peak concurrent player count sits at 822,361. That immediately places the release among the most popular games currently on the store, outstripping the all-time records of Marvel Rivals and Battlefield 6, and even the 24-hour peaks of stalwarts like PUBG and the omni-present Bongo Cat.

At time of writing, nearly 400,000 are playing on the PC marketplace. A healthy, robust audience was ready and waiting for this game, it seems.

Drawing on wuxia, a genre of Chinese storytelling that fuses martial arts and fantasy elements, Phantom Blade Zero involves you trying to help an assassin clear his name after he's framed for a murder by the organization he works for. The history Chinese setting looks gorgeous and the martial arts-infused combat seems like a tonne of fun.

Donnie Yen is involved, and part of me likes to think he's a driving force behind the emphatic playerbase. We're unlikely to ever get an Ip Man game, but we have this, and it's close enough, in all honesty.

#4043. FBI investigating theft of more than 6000 PSA-graded trading cards, including almost 3000 Pokémon cards

"Recovering every stolen item and returning it to its owner is our top priority."

The FBI and Santa Ana police are investigating the theft of 6451 PSA-graded cards, including nearly 3000 Pokémon cards, from a FedEx truck in California.

PSA confirmed the investigation, saying the orders were stolen on 13th October from a FedEx truck after pickup at its Santa Ana facility.

The company says that "recovering every stolen item and returning it to its owner is our top priority", and that it has given investigators video footage, shipment manifests, and item-level records.

In total, 6451 items were taken. PSA has published a list of every stolen card, including its certification number and, for serialised cards, the serial number. It deactivated the certification numbers and shared the list with marketplace sellers, auction houses, and digital commerce platforms, so the cards can't be easily resold.

According to TheGamer, which broke down the list by category, Pokémon cards account for 2978 of the stolen items, followed by 898 One Piece cards, 880 basketball cards, 640 baseball cards, and 433 football cards. The New York Times reports that the haul is collectively worth more than $963,000.

PSA has refunded the grading fees on all affected orders, and says these refunds are separate from compensation for the cards themselves. Orders sent with a PSA return label are covered by its insurance, with payments already going out. Customers who used their own label will work with a dedicated PSA team, and those who bought through a dealer should contact them directly. Compensation is based on fair market value, up to each item's declared maximum insured value, and customers can choose to return the item if it is recovered.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the FBI's Los Angeles office or Santa Ana police.

In July, Cheshire Police confirmed that brothers Keith and Shane Johnson had been caught after breaking into Celestial Collectables and stealing Pokémon cards to the value of £62,000.

#4042. "IT FLIPS UP," Fallout New Vegas modders yell after releasing a funky Pip-Boy based on cancelled entry Van Buren's design docs

The same folks are hard at work remaking Van Buren as part of a project dubbed Fallout: The New West

One of the days last week was October 23rd. It's the date in the Fallout universe when the bombs dropped and has morphed into a time for yearly community happenings plus, in Bethesda's case, usually some marketing. Sometimes, modders behind long-running projects time up standalone releases with it, as has been the case this year with the folks behind Fallout: The New West, the project aiming to make their own version of Black Isle Studios' cancelled third Fallout game. They've released a few guns inspired by the canned entry, which you may know by its codename Van Buren, but the headliner from this gear drop for New Vegas is a funky new Pip-Boy design.

According to its creators, this Lil Pip 3000 iteration of Fallout's iconic wrist-mounted computer has been recreated based on Van Buren's original design docs. Worn by inmates in Tibbets Prison, the AI overlord-run slammer that the modders have already recreated for a demo of their Van Buren remake, the Lil Pip has made its way to Mojave in the hands of an unnamed ranger who's deposited it near Nipton.

It does all the standard Pip-Boy things and should work with a host of established mods which add extra features to The Courier's fancy bracelet. Most importantly of all, thanks to custom animations, the lid flips up when you whip the device out to use it. To be clear since the modders have emphasised this in all caps, I said "IT FLIPS UP". In all seriousness, it's a cool design that departs from the general blockiness of the default Pip-Boys worn by Fallout protagonists old and new. It's perhaps heavier on children's toy vibes than its siblings, but not to the extent I'd say it looks like it couldn't survive its wearer failing to step out of the way of a rogue missile or grenade.

Alongside it, the New West lot have released a Wattz Weapon Pack. Consisting of five laser guns in the classic Fallout style, including a freshly assembled burst pistol from Van Buren, the mod also includes custom animations and add-ons to help these new energy weapons fit in seamlessly with the rest of New Vegas' arsenal. They'll even be distributed throughout the Capital Wasteland if you're running the Tale of Two Wastelands mod which mashes New Vegas and Fallout 3's worldspaces together.

If you fancy nabbing either mod, you'll need to nab a fair few requirements. The New Vegas Script Extender, JIP LN NVSE Plugin, JohnnyGuitar NVSE, and kNVSE Animation Plugin are musts for both, while the weapon pack also needs the Gun Runners’ Arsenal DLC, ShowOff xNVSE Plugin, ISControl Enabler, and Sound Extender.

Godzilla Minus Zero doubles the kaiju, but still has human stakes, according to director Takashi Yamazaki

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Godzilla Minus Zero director Takashi Yamazaki has explained that, even though his highly anticipated sequel film introduces King Ghidorah, it's so much more than a mere kaiju brawl.

The film is a follow-up to Godzilla Minus One, which was widely praised for its human story – and in the sequel, the Shikishima family will be back.

"I didn't want Minus Zero to turn into this giant pro wrestling match of watching two kaiju on screen," Yamazaki told SFX magazine in the latest issue. "There's still a very strong relationship between humans and the kaiju. How that unfolds and translates into drama – the lines are much more blurred, shall we say?

"[Ghidorah] really shifts the human's perspective of what kaiju are and how to approach them," he continued. "It's no longer just hatred. It's a much more complex and complicated relationship that humans now have with them. In that sense, the kaiju also embody this almost natural disaster type of entity within them, like this force of nature that cannot be reckoned with or negotiated with, to a degree.

"If you look at Japan, it's a country that's been hit by earthquakes, typhoons and a lot of natural disasters," he added. "It's coexisting with natural disasters, living in Japan. So the characters watching Godzilla or [Ghidorah] duke it out is a very complex feeling. Perhaps it's very Japanese in its approach, but I think that's what makes the Japanese line of Godzilla different from the Hollywood version."

The film has already debuted to a near-perfect Rotten Tomatoes score, and our own Godzilla Minus Zero review awards it 4.5 stars. "With devastating human drama and earth-shaking kaiju action, Godzilla Minus Zero ups the ante in every way from its predecessor – and is easily one of the best films of the year," it reads.

Godzilla Minus Zero arrives this November 6. For more, check out our guide to all the upcoming movies left of 2026.

Jack Lowden is staying tight-lipped on his Bond prospects

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The race for the next James Bond is heating up, with four finalists currently being tested for the most coveted role in movies. One candidate is Slow Horses star Jack Lowden, but the Scottish actor recently threw cold water on the suggestion he will be the next 007.

Speaking to British GQ, Lowden was inevitably quizzed about being subject to the relentless Bond rumor mill, only to "suck" his teeth in response. "On this… It’s all very flattering. It’s nice to be mentioned – for any role – and I’m just not really going to add to the noise." British GQ described the response as a "bucket of cold water, poured with care."

Back in September, Lowden's Slow Horses co-star Gary Oldman said the next Bond had already been cast, pointedly adding that Lowden was on the shortlist. Oldman later walked back the comments on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, but where there's smoke there's fire, and numerous reports since have identified Lowden as one of the final four.

“It’s very nice, and Gary’s a sweetheart," Lowden said of Oldman's comments. "It's particularly lovely, coming from someone like him. But I don’t really listen to it. As a young male actor, generally, the minute you’re not playing a zany artist type, the minute you’re in a suit, people fling it at you."

The other Bond potentials reportedly include Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, and a mystery fourth actor who has yet to be identified. While Lowden is something of a fan-favorite choice, having already played a British spy on the long-running Apple TV series Slow Horses, Lowden's many Apple TV commitments could be a potential hurdle to the star playing Bond. Not only is season 7 of Slow Horses in production for next year, but season 8 has already been confirmed, with Lowden's River Cartwright expected to appear in both (despite that season 6 cliffhanger). Lowden is also set to appear in Apple TV's series adaptation of Berlin Noir alongside Colin Firth, potentially leaving little time to play Bond.

If Lowden is cast as the next 007, the perfect Bond villain is sitting right there, as Lowden's real-life wife Saoirse Ronan has said she's "dead serious" about playing a Bond villain.

Slow Horses season 6 is currently streaming on Apple TV. For more, check out our ranking of the best James Bond movies.

#4037. God of War's Dave Bautista Beefs Up 9kg for Kratos TV Show Role

Dave Bautista has been busy in the gym after being cast as Kratos in Amazon Prime’s upcoming live action God of War adaptation.

Showing off in a branded shirt on social media, the former wrestler confirmed he’d put on 20lbs in muscle to play the role. That’s about 9kgs for those of you outside of the US.

The 57-year-old now weighs 250lbs (113kg), so is an absolute beefcake considering his age. He’s also 6’6” so certainly has the imposing presence required to play the protagonist.

Bautista is taking over the role from Ryan Hurst, who got injured during filming earlier in the year.

While I obviously sympathise with the original actor, I think Bautista is an upgrade – and he’s clearly put in the work to build the physique required to represent the character.

I’m excited to see the first photos of him in full makeup, with Kratos’ iconic red “lightning strike” tattoo.

#4036. 220,000-signatory petition to "save Mass Effect" doesn't mention BioWare, suggests giving Mass Effect 5 to somebody else

Expanse devs Owlcat join call for EA to let Mass Effect "flourish anew"

The word "BioWare" does not appear in a recent Change.org petition asking EA to "save Mass Effect", which has gained around 220,000 signatories as of writing. The nearest the petition gets is an allusion to "recent revelations" that have "cast a shadow over its future", which is a remarkably gentle way of saying that the parent company shanked the creators to balance their books, after going into historic debt.

Still, one can hardly reproach the petition organisers for not mentioning BioWare - after all, EA announced that they were closing BioWare a whole four days ago, and the funeral baked meats must coldly furnish forth the pitchdeck. There are other videogame studios, aren't there? Just get one of them to make the thing. Maybe Owlcat, developers of the Mass Effect-flavoured The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, who've shared the Change.org petition on their socials.

I'm sure the HashtagSaveMassEffect petition was written out of sincere love for an absorbingly written epic sci-fi soap opera in which a charismatic group of weirdos unpick a wonderful cosmic conspiracy. Doubtless, many recently laid-off Mass Effect devs will be touched by their enthusiasm. Doubtless, I am being a pissy old crank. Still, the officious and press-releasey, 'gamer CEO' language of the petition makes my skin crawl. It reads like it was written by three 12-year-old boys standing on each other's shoulders inside a pinstripe suit.

"The decline in dedicated resources and ambiguous development plans from Electronic Arts (EA) threaten to leave this beloved series at a standstill, jeopardizing its incredible legacy," it pines. "Fans around the globe have invested thousands of hours exploring the galaxy, forming deep connections with its multifaceted characters and compelling storylines.

"It is a franchise that has transcended the typical gamer experience, creating a community that advocates for choice, individuality, and shared adventure," the petitioners write. "The potential cessation of new developments in this universe is a devastating prospect not only for fans but for the diversity of narrative-driven games as a whole.

"Therefore, we are urgently petitioning EA to take decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect," it continues. "This commitment requires proper funding, adequate staffing, and time allocation to maintain and advance the high standards the franchise is known for. Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property (IP) to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

Getting a third party to make it? I'm sure the idea has never occurred to EA, and nor has it ever occurred to them that they could get a third party to make it for cheaper. Although if the testimony of former employees is any indication, it's likely they'll just end up sitting on the unfinished Mass Effect 5 forever.

I don't think either the Change.org petitioner or the signatories are genuinely devoid of all sympathy for the BioWare devs who lost their jobs last week. I wish them the best getting the credit-sozzled chatbot-humpers up the ladder to keep developers in work, though I do have some words of advice: the execs will not be impressed by your homages to go-faster marketing terminology like "passion", "vision" and the "investment" of your leisure time. They will regard this only as proof that they've successfully mind-fucked you into thinking like them. They will applaud your language's tendency to hail products as eternal and workers as interchangeable.

Still, shying away from even mentioning BioWare, while freshly jettisoned devs air their abandoned plans for Mass Effect 5, is just kind of weird! If you have such a "deep connection" with these games, the least you can do is name the people who made them, and maybe talk a little about how things got this bad.

#4035. An officially licensed Knightmare game, based on the British TV show, is coming next year

A free point-and-click adventure based on Knightmare, the cult ITV children's show, is in development.

The officially licensed game, complete with the original voice cast, is being made by a team led by writer and designer Ewen Watson, with show creator Tim Child giving the project his blessing. It’s due on PC next year to mark the show’s 40th anniversary. Here's a peek:

For the uninitiated, Knightmare aired on ITV between 1987 and 1994 and single-handedly introduced an entire generation of kids to fantasy RPGs and computer games. Sitting with Treguard, the deeply affable Dungeon Master, three kids in ironed jeans and their best button-up shirts would direct a fourth member of their team, the Dungeoneer, through a labyrinthine hand-painted dungeon, solving riddles, casting spells, and - hopefully - avoiding traps.

Interestingly, the players' life force meter - the stuff of legend of (k)nightmare fuel - has been ditched in a bid to give players the time they need to explore.

Much of its cast is returning, including Hugo Myatt as Treguard, Mark Knight as Lord Fear, Clifford Barry as Brother Strange, Edmund Dehn as Gumboil the Knight, Iona Kennedy as Greystagg, and Paul Valentine and Alec Westwood as jesters Motley and Folly, respectively.

Watson says the game's art was drawn by hand, stressing "everything you see and hear is made by real humans" (thanks, VGC).

It'll be a short adventure - Watson estimates suggest it'll take just a couple of hours to finish - and because its free-to-play, sadly there are no plans to bring it to consoles.

The TV show returned in a special one-off episode on YouTube 13(!) years ago.

The item shop token in Fortnite is exceedingly rare, so here's everything you need to know about it

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Fortnite pirate shop token is currently the talk of the town, as it represents an incredible piece of plundered loot to tie in with the piracy-themed mini-season. If you're lucky enough to find this extremely rare token during Fortnite Treasure Hunters, then you'll be able to plunder the item shop by claiming almost everything available there for free during a two week period, making this one of the most valuable rewards ever! To bring you up to speed, I'll explain how to get a pirate shop token in Fortnite and how rare it actually is.

Currently, the only way to get a Fortnite pirate shop token is to keep opening chests in the game, as it is a random loot drop. It comes from standard chests, so you don't need to track down rare ones, and you'll know if you've found an item shop token as the chest will glow and shake for several seconds before exploding with a "YOU FOUND PIRATE SHOP ACCESS" message appearing across the screen.

If you're lucky enough to discover this you'll actually receive two items – PIRATE SHOP ACCESS (2026) and PIRATE SHOP ACCESS (2027). The first needs to be activated by December 15, 2026, while the second will become available next year, and once redeemed they allow you to claim anything sold for V-Bucks in the Fortnite Item Shop for free for 14 days. This excludes passes levels, gifting, and real money bundles, and you can only claim one free sidekick you don't own already, but otherwise you can absolutely stuff your locker with a huge amount of free cosmetics!

MIGHT BE THE FIRST EVER PIRATE SHOP ACCESS IM GOING CRAZY OMG #Fortnite #FortniteCh7S4 https://t.co/lZJ01OkYLwNovember 1, 2026

Naturally for such a valuable reward, the Fortnite pirate shop token is incredibly rare and at the time of writing only one player has reportedly found it. You can increase your odds of discovering a token by playing with friends, as if one member of a duo, trio, or squad finds this elusive item then everyone else in the group will also receive it. Otherwise, all you can do is continue searching as many chests as possible and keeping everything crossed – good luck and happy hunting!

#4033. Feature: 25 Years Later, How Many Of These Original Xbox Launch Titles Have You Played?

From the original North American launch on November 15, 2001

Welcome to the month of Xbox's 25th anniversary! Xbox will be celebrating that milestone officially on November 15th, but before we get there, we thought we'd use the chance to highlight the very first games that ever launched on Xbox.

To do that, we're going back to the initial list of North American Xbox launch titles, of which there were 20 in all. Some of them are obvious standouts, such as Halo: Combat Evolved, Fuzion Frenzy, Dead or Alive 3 and Project Gotham Racing, while others are more obscure - Arctic Thunder, Dark Summit, Mad Dash Racing, etc.

Here's the full list of all 20 launch titles:

Now, of course, some of these games are still playable to this day on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, while others have always remained locked to the original Xbox. The likes of Project Gotham Racing, Shrek and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2x are highly-requested additions to the Xbox backwards compatibility library, but it seems unlikely they'll ever make the cut at this point - almost certainly due to licensing reasons.

However, you may not know that games like Cel Damage and Oddworld: Munch's Oddysee are still playable to this day on modern consoles, and they're still well worth checking out despite their age.

So, how many of these original Xbox launch titles have you played? Let us know down in the comments section below, and please do give us your recommendations with some of the obscure ones - NHL Hitz is still one of my faves!

#4032. Steam's AI disclosures are akin to "forcing developers to list their voting history", says man who must hate seeing eggs virtue signal that they're free-range

Tim Sweeney's throwing a wobbler in the supermarket

How could someone do this to you, fruit, meat, and other foods on the shelves of this shop? You've been forced, in a horrific crime against the companies responsible for you, to reveal some details about how you were produced. No, this isn't reasonable information to offer a would-be purchaser, so that they can feel more comfortable and confident in knowing what they're about to spend their hard-earned money on. It's a bat signal for the anti-battery farming hate mobs and is robbing innocent food producers of their ability to rake in cash without having to reveal some basic info about their products. You might as well stick "mandatory political essays" on the packaging of frozen peas!

This, I imagine based on recent comments he's made about Steam's requirement that games made using generative AI disclose that via a brief blurb on their store pages, is how Tim Sweeney feels every time he goes to stock up his cupboards. Since declaring that Epic are going all-in on genAI and unveiling a new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher, the Sweens has been pro-AI posting with reckless abandon. On one hand, eeewwwwww, on the other, it's a chance for the rest of us to think about what it might be a good idea for games to disclose beyond any genAI use.

Yep, fooled you. This isn't going to be 400 words of me just clowning on Tim. Some of it definitely is that (hello, opening paragraph), but not all of it.

First of all, what the Sweens said. "Forcing developers to write a political statement to be used against them by the hate mob they’re helping organize is abhorrent," he posted late last week in response to some AI bloke declaring Steam's genAI disclosures absurd. "Age ratings tell parents what’s in a game so they can make informed decisions for their kids," Sweeney continued in the thread which developed. "These AI statements are just as partisan as mandatory political essays or forcing developers to list their voting history to drive cancel campaigns and public struggle sessions.

Age ratings tell parents what’s in a game so they can make informed decisions for their kids.These AI statements are just as partisan as mandatory political essays or forcing developers to list their voting history to drive cancel campaigns and public struggle sessions.

"There is a real economic cost to Valve’s foray into forced political disclosures. Besides taking 30%, they’re also taking a potentially even larger fraction of developers’ revenue and livelihood by undermining their business with these AI hate campaigns." The Sweens also batted away someone pointing out that Epic-owned asset marketplace Fab asks creators to disclose genAI use via tags, claiming that it being a B2B platform makes it a totally different kettle of fish, seemingly because one of those fish might sue Epic if they ended up unwittingly buying AI-generated stuff to stick in their game.

You're getting off lucky, Sweens. Imagine if studios' store pages had to disclose details like how many hours of mandatory dev overtime went into getting a game over the line, the size of their gender pay gap, or, god forbid, how much the publisher's top exec earned throughout development in comparison to the median worker or lowest ranking junior! Maybe a quick breakdown of how many of the devs weren't white dudes. None of those, on paper, would force studios to write a political essay explaining why they've done whatever they've done or why the numbers look as they do. Though, you might feel compelled to pen something if, say, you know that you're operating in a way that'll put off most of your customer base unless you're allowed to hide it.

#4031. Elden Ring movie has a budget of nearly $200 million

A24's live-action Elden Ring movie is reportedly set to cost almost $200 million, making it the most expensive film the studio has ever made.

The figure comes from a new report in the Wall Street Journal, and suggests there's been a big jump from earlier reports in April, which then put the budget at "well over" $100 million.

For context, A24's priciest film to date, Marty Supreme, reportedly cost around $70 million, a step up from Alex Garland's Civil War at about $50 million.

The WSJ's piece is less about Elden Ring than about A24's growing clout in Hollywood and the rivals now chasing its success.

"They're a Goldilocks company. Just the right amount of people doing just the right amount of things," Telluride Film Festival director Julie Huntsinger told the paper (thanks, IG).

Garland is writing and directing the adaptation, which is being shot for IMAX and is due in cinemas on 3rd March 2028. Kit Connor, Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, Tom Burke, Havana Rose Liu, Sonoya Mizuno, Jonathan Pryce, and Nick Offerman are among the cast.

FromSoftware's open-world action RPG launched in February 2022, with lore written by Game of Thrones author George RR Martin.

Production on Alex Garland's Elden Ring movie - which is, at least partially, a prequel to FromSoftware's RPG - seems to be progressing well. Even Dung Eater is seemingly in, so fans are expecting a rather faithful adaptation. Now, the latest set video suggests some low-level enemies will show up too.

Over the summer, a video leak of the real set Conwy Castle, North Wales. A few familiar human soldiers - probably before the Shattering occurs - were atop the walls and towers, guarding the location and patrolling. And back in April, North Wales Pioneer teased Alex Garland's feature would shoot there.

#4030. Phoenix Cyclops Is Available Now as Marvel Tokon Receives Major PS5 Patch

The first post-launch DLC character for Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is now available. Phoenix Cyclops joins the fun today, 2nd November 2026, and he's accompanied by a major game update that makes a ton of improvements.

Those who own the Year 1 Pass will already have access to Phoenix Cyclops, but he's also available as a standalone purchase, costing $7.99/£6.49.

There are also a couple of premium costumes available for purchase. There's a "Classic" blue and yellow outfit for Cyclops, while Hulk gets a Joe Fixit costume. They each sell for $4.99/£3.99.

As mentioned, Phoenix Cyclops brings with him a major game update, free for all players, that fixes and improves the overall experience.

Improvements have been implemented regarding online play and cross-play with the PC version which should make online multiplayer more stable.

There are also fixes and updates to Training mode, some Character Lessons, and numerous characters.

Probably the biggest thing, though, is a pretty big change to certain game mechanics, mostly focused around assists.

In a nutshell, developer Arc System Works has reduced the frequency you can summon and tag into allies, forcing players to play neutral/with a singular character at times and to improve legibility during a match.

The patch notes are extensive — you can read the whole lot through the link if you're interested.

Hideo Kojima rejected a Metal Gear Solid anime 20 years ago, but the developer's tune must have changed with Disney's Death Stranding anime on the way

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After announcing the anime at Disney Plus' Originals Preview last year, Hideo Kojima revealed the first trailer for his upcoming Death Stranding Isolations show last week, based in the same universe as his hit Death Stranding video game series.

However, the news has made fans think back to when the developer rejected a pitch for a Metal Gear Solid anime over two decades earlier. "Metal Gear Solid is the neglected child," said one fan on Twitter, thinking of what could have been.

Back in 2021, Toonami co-founder Jason DeMarco took to Twitter and revealed he once tried to pitch an anime series to the Metal Gear Solid creator. "About a year after Metal Gear Solid came out, I met with Kojima and discussed the idea of making a Metal Gear anime. I talked about how much I loved the games and what the anime might be like," said DeMarco in a Tweet that has since been deleted, but was shared by ComicBook.

It sounds like Kojima didn't like the idea at all, as DeMarco said the developer responded by pointing at him and saying "Otaku" before breaking out into laughter. For reference, otaku is a Japanese word used to describe someone who is obsessed with a certain subject, often anime and manga. DeMarco added that the response made him laugh as well. But alas, the Metal Gear Solid anime never came to be.

Released in 1998, Metal Gear Solid follows former Special Forces operative Solid Snake as he is pulled out of retirement by the US government to go undercover and infiltrate a nuclear weapons facility that has been taken over by a rogue unit. Players must free the hostages and prevent the unit from using the compound armor weapon known as Metal Gear REX. Perhaps DeMarco was just ahead of its time, as the video game adaptation genre has gone through somewhat of a renaissance in the past few years, and there are most certainly grounds for a juicy story there.

Who knows, maybe Kojima will rethink his decision after Death Stranding Isolations hits streaming in 2027. The anime series focuses on a new story away from the video games, following a young man and woman as they set out on an adventure in search of human connection after a catastrophic event, as per the official synopsis.

For more, check out the other new anime coming your way next year.

#4028. With Xbox cuts not done, Microsoft offer voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 workers across the company in latest attempt to get rid of staff

That's around a quarter of Microsoft’s total workforce, according to reports

Update: According to Vertical Slice and The Verge, an unspecified number of Xbox staff are among those who've been offered voluntary buyouts by Microsoft.

Staff at Microsoft continue to recieve emails they'd probably rather not be getting. After telling some the other week of plans to mandate four days in the office starting in February and presiding over multiple rounds of layoffs at their gaming division Xbox, Microsoft are now offering volutary buyouts to 60,000, roughly 25% of their overall headcount.

Business Insider report that staff in the US, Canada, India, and the UK, but that not every team within the company is on the eligibility list. There's no indication at current as to whether Xbox will be affected, with exec Matt Booty having noted when announcing September's layoffs that the division was "roughly three-quarters of the way" through efforts to get rid of 3200 staff in total. According a report last week, further Xbox cuts were being planned for this month, November and January.

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman wrote in a memo to staff. "This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.

"The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We’ll learn from it. At the same time, we’ll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute."

According to Business Insider, 9000 staff were offered buyouts in the previous voluntary retirement program Coleman mentioned, with around a third taking it.

Solidarity to Microsoft staff affected by this latest attempt to fire people into the sun, reportedly as a result of Microsoft straining to pour boatloads of money into AI data centers.

As of writing, Microsoft are still subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#4027. Call of Duty movie will explore the "cost of war", says director

The Call of Duty movie will explore "the cost of war" and probably won't be as graphically violent as director Peter Berg's upcoming Netflix film, The Mosquito Bowl.

In an interview with ComicBook, Berg, who is directing from a script by Taylor Sheridan, said the Modern Warfare games the film draws on are about more than shooting.

Berg said that underneath the hardware and killing, the games are "really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry".

He described the characters - Captain Price, Soap, Ghost, and Alex - as "complicated humans", not "cartoon characters or comic books", and said there's "a real soul" beneath the violence.

"This is not just 'Hey, let's shoot them all up and shoot popcorn!' Like, there's a soul underneath it, that I understand that Taylor Sheridan understands, and I think probably not quite as graphically violent as Mosquito Bowl, but there will be a very strong soul, and consequence of war within the film, called 'duty,'" he said.

Berg's Mosquito Bowl, a Second World War drama inspired by a real 1944 football match between Marines in the Pacific, arrives on Netflix on 25th November. The Call of Duty movie is due in cinemas on 30th June 2028.

A former long-time Call of Duty developer recently called out Activision executives profiteering from the re-release of games like Black Ops 1 and 2, whereas the developers who contributed "blood, sweat, and tears" to make them gained nothing.

#4026. OG Xbox Game 'Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee' Gets Remastered, But What Do The Critics Think?

Was it worth digging the original Xbox title back up?

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee launched on the original Xbox in 2003, a few months after its GameCube debut, and sadly, only in North America. The kaiju arena-brawler, which depicted the iconic King of Monsters, Godzilla, body-slamming Ghidorah into various cityscapes, has apparently made a big enough impact to warrant Atari funding a remaster in 2026.

Sadly, the whole North American release made it quite difficult for us Brits to get our mucky mitts on the game, and DAMM wasn't a big enough deal for Xbox to share the game with the rest of the world. DAMM did get the backward compatibility treatment, however, only on Xbox 360, and again restricted to North America.

I guess then, we're quite pleased Atari decided to take a punt on a DAMM remaster. Even though it seems to share many of the original's downfalls, Godzilla's WWE antics are going to be available on November 3rd on Xbox Series X|S, and best of all, I can play it from my lovely little home in Cornwall.

So, here's what the critics are saying about Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered:

"Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered brings the classic kaiju brawler roaring back with impressive rebuilt visuals, satisfying arena destruction, and chaotic multiplayer battles. While its limited roster and tedious character unlocks feel dated, the accessible combat and faithful Godzilla presentation make this a thoroughly entertaining return for the King of the Monsters."

"Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered feels like a new game with its graphical upgrade, held back slightly by a lack of any other meaningful new additions and a somewhat grindy gameplay loop."

"Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a satisfyingly faithful update to a beloved Kaiju brawler. It’s simple and fun, with local and online multiplayer keeping you around for the long haul despite a wafer-thin single-player experience. Now if we could just get a remaster of Save The Earth and Unleashed."

Review Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered (Switch 2) - The King Returns With A Fun But Thin Kaiju Brawler

"Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is at its best when it simulates the idea of smashing kaiju toys together as a kid in short sessions with friends, and at its worst when it attempts to prolong a game that never had much depth to begin with. The result is a remaster I’m glad exists considering the drought of Godzilla brawlers, but with a few caveats–not to mention the sting of realizing that the original GameCube and Xbox game were absent of arbitrary grinding."

"Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered remains goofy fun, and Atari’s remaster looks and runs well. It’s still a rather simple game and probably not the most comprehensive when it comes to the characters and lore. But it’s a good time and offers quite a few different modes to get acclimated and beat up famous faces."

"Right now, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a great version of a good retro game. Because the game was remade from the ground up, I wish the developers had made a super version of the Godzilla trilogy with more content. While Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered’s combat is really fun, there’s not much depth. There are lots of modes, and a bit of RPG unlocking, but this isn’t a deep fighting game that’s going to be played at tournaments. It’s a great budget buy for Godzilla fans. But more content would have made Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered a more obvious recommendation. If you’re at all curious, or have any fondness for the original game, it remains a fun time."

"In the media shadow of sacred monsters like Grand Theft Auto VI and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, only an equally fearless monstrosity could face them: Godzilla. Nearly a quarter century after its release on GameCube, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee returns with a remaster that discreetly refreshes the audiovisual experience and improves the progression without betraying its structure. The core is that of a 3D fighting game in which kaiju clashes are accompanied by the destruction of entire cities, in a blaze of explosions and particle effects. Behind this chaos lies a combat system that's immediate, but not always precise and balanced, suspended somewhere between classic fighting games and the festive jumble of a party game. The mechanics are simple, despite a certain unwieldiness in the movements, and the best of the action is found especially in local multiplayer."

Well, there you have it, folks! Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is an almost perfect example of a good '7' rated game. At the time of writing, the remaster is holding down a 72 score on Metacritic.

What's interesting is that the original Xbox release scored 73 on Metacritic - a single point higher than the remaster. It's funny how 23 years can pass and a game can be reviewed almost identically.

Milsim and Non Milsim Content in Modern Warfare 4 are new labels in multiplayer, but what does that mean?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Non-Milsim Content in MW4 is a new kind of warning label that players can find attached to multiplayer game modes like Possession, but what does it actually mean for something in COD to be Milsim Content or not? If your familiarity with Call of Duty games and military shooters is more casual, you might not be familiar with this term, but here's what you can expect when it comes up in MW4 multiplayer.

Non-Milsim Content in MW4 is a warning label on certain game modes in multiplayer, and what it basically means is that this particular game mode isn't going to be very realistic to military combat. Whether that's a good thing or a bad thing is up to you.

Milsim is a gaming term that's shorthand for "Military Simulation", a reference to Call of Duty's declared genre, as well as similar games in the industry like Battlefield. Obviously you can argue about how realistic they actually are, but in this case the label "Non Milsim Content" is tied to multiplayer modes that specifically aren't interested in anything like actual realism. For example, the limited time Halloween "Possession" mode allows you to leap into the bodies of enemies you kill and control them, which clearly isn't grounded in any sort of realism.

You can still bring your own guns into Possession, even if there's a risk of them being commandeered by the enemy. #4024. Final Fantasy Resonance Producer Had to Fight Square Enix Execs Who Wanted Cheap Port of Dead Mobile Game

Final Fantasy Resonance has seemingly gone down really, really well with fans of the franchise — and so it's surprising to hear that Square Enix's leadership were apparently against the idea of the game.

Resonance is very much a callback to classic Final Fantasy in terms of gameplay and structure; some would go as far to argue that it's just what the property needs at this point.

The recently released and highly rated RPG is built on the bones of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius — the mobile gacha game that was shut down back in 2024.

However, Resonance reworks entire systems to ensure that everything functions as you'd expect of a traditional Final Fantasy adventure. After playing it myself for review, it's clear that the development team put a lot of effort into essentially remaking Exvius.

But according to project producer Keisuke Nakashima, his higher-ups wanted a simple port of Exvius rather than the extensive adaptation that we ended up with.

Review Final Fantasy Resonance (PS5) - Square's Series Returns to Its Roots to Fantastic Effect

He told Bloomberg (via Nintendo Everything): "Initially there was some resistance to the idea from Square Enix executives [...] I didn’t want to go down that route. I wanted to create an original version for consoles that was a full-blown gameplay experience.”

The suggestion is that a straightforward port would have cost much less to produce. At the time of writing, we don't know how well Resonance has sold.

Still, I'm glad Nakashima held his ground, because I'm not even sure how an Exvius port would have worked in the first place. It certainly wouldn't have hit like Resonance does.

#4023. The GameMaker engine series behind Undertale, Hotline Miami and Spelunky is going free for commercial use on PC

Here's some upbeat news to end the day on (unless one of the other awful people working here posts something diabolical, once I'm done) - you'll soon be able to publish games created using the latest GameMaker tools for free on PC alongside web and mobile.

Hitherto, game developers have needed a Professional license to sell or monetise GameMaker creations. That changes on 1st January 2027. You'll still need a paid license if you plan to release a GameMaker game on console, but pish posh, those things are going extinct anyway.

In case you're unfamiliar, GameMaker is a series of game creation tools that dates back around 26 years. Current developers YoYo Games – who are now owned by browser company Opera - announced that they would make the tools free for non-commercial use on PC in November 2023, bringing a rare grimace of affection to former RPS archchancellor Graham Smith's time-poisoned visage. I can only imagine his happily beaming mug right now.

GameMaker has been used by such indie noteworthies as Heart Machine (Hyper Light Drifter), Toby Fox (Undertale), Derek Yu (Spelunky, UFO 50), Vlambeer (Nuclear Throne), and Dennaton Games (Hotline Miami). And also by Graham, apparently, though I'm not sure what he was using it for. It's historically been aimed more at novice programmers (see also: Graham), with a focus on 2D visuals, though the latest incarnation, GameMaker Runtime, aims to beef up the toolset's 3D capabilities.

Community dev Ross Manthorpe detailed the change in a post on the official site, explaining the implications for people who currently have a Pro license. "Developers who currently own the Professional license will still be able to commercially distribute games made on the existing GMS2 runtime, and will additionally benefit from access to GMS2 runtime source code," he wrote. "Regardless of runtime, developers will still need an Enterprise license and to be an approved developer to be able to export to consoles. There will be no changes to existing tier pricing."

Any devs here partial to GameMaker? I've been faffing around with Twine recently, and wondering whether I dare experiment with something that supports Proper Graphics. Perhaps in a few years time, some other RPS writer will be casually roasting my efforts at GameMaking, the way I have just made fun of poor Graham. Poor Graham! *camps entrance to comments with rocket launcher*

#4022. 187K+ fans call for EA to "Save Mass Effect"

A petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, has topped 187,000 signatures.

We said a sad farewell to BioWare earlier this week. Job cuts, coming just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of the company, were anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".

"This commitment requires proper funding, adequate staffing, and time allocation to maintain and advance the high standards the franchise is known for," the Change.Org page reads.

"Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property (IP) to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

The petition adds: "Fans around the globe have invested thousands of hours exploring the galaxy, forming deep connections with its multifaceted characters and compelling storylines. It is a franchise that has transcended the typical gamer experience, creating a community that advocates for choice, individuality, and shared adventure. The potential cessation of new developments in this universe is a devastating prospect not only for fans but for the diversity of narrative-driven games as a whole."

Yesterday, we reported that a content creator claiming to have served on a BioWare community council shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.

#4021. Boltgun 2 and Warhammer Survivors devs Auroch Digital say they're laying off 25% of their staff in now-deleted posts

Not long after releasing boomer shooter Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun II and right before Warhammer Survivors launches in November, developers Auroch Digital have unfortunately given a public statement confirming that roughly a quarter of its current staff will be laid off as part of a restructuring. What's strange — to the point that layoffs are, unfortunately, expected — is that the initial social media posts, on both LinkedIn and Twitter, have now been deleted.

In the studio's statement, posted yesterday, Auroch notes their pride in Boltgun II and Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War, both released this year, but "despite that creative success, the same market conditions that have challenged so many of our fellow developers have now also affected us." Apologies to the staff affected follow, with a plea "to partners and friends in the industry: if you are hiring, please consider finding a place for our staff in your studio. They have worked on everything from indie shooters to AAA [co-development], and their talent and breadth is second-to-none." The studio also confirms that post-launch development on both Boltgun II and Warhammer Survivors will continue despite the loss of staff.

This is, sadly, not an uncommon thing to report on by any means. There are layoffs every goddamn week, if not several. This is unique, though, in that in the time between the post going up yesterday and my writing of this piece, the public statements have been deleted. There's an archive of the original image posted here, as you won't find it on Auroch's Twitter or LinkedIn anymore. Even with the barrage of layoff news, I can't think of another time that a statement has been outright retracted within a day. Whether this was posted in error, too early, or some other reason I can't know of, hopefully there'll be some clarity soon and, more importantly, opportunities available for the staff affected.

RPS have reached out to Auroch Digital for comment and clarification.

#4020. Canadian political party leader blames BioWare's closure on private equity, says government should help former employees buy it back

"This is what it does. Buy up businesses, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for short-term profit."

In the wake of EA's tragic shuttering of BioWare last week, a leader of one of Canada's New Democratic Party has spoken out about the perils of private equity, and said BioWare employees should be able to buy the studio with "federal support".

Avi Lewis, head of Canada's NDP, took to Bluesky to decry the news of BioWare's closure. He wrote: "This is private equity, this is what it does. Buy up businesses, run them into the ground, and rip them apart for short-term profit."

He then moves on to the idea of a studio buyback, writing: "The developers at BioWare know how to run the studio. They know how to make the games we all love. They should be given the first opportunity - and the federal support - to buy it and run it themselves."

The combined statement against private equity and for the BioWare employees is no coincidence. EA was recently acquired through a record-breaking leveraged buyout by Saudi Arabia's Savvy Games Group as well as US president Donald Trump's Son-in-law Jared Kushner's private equity firm. Months later, not only did BioWare close, but 400 employees lost their jobs across a variety of studios including Respawn, Maxis, Full Circle, and more.

We're seeing a growing number of politicians speak on the video game industry issues in recent years. In September, a Mexican lawmaker pushed for better consumer rights for digital goods in the wake of Sony's push away from discs. Late last year, a similar situation occurred, where Concord's swift shutdown was brought up in British parliament, in a discussion on consumer rights protections, as was Rockstar's ongoing tribunal involving fired workers. This is perhaps not surprising, as a new generation of more digitally aware politicians come into positions of influence and the need to appeal to younger voters invested in the video games industry becomes more necessary.

Lewis was far from the only person to share their thoughts on BioWare's closure. Many across the games industry shared their sadness ,frustration, and support last week. This included key figures from Larian, CD Projekt Red, and even Warren Spector.

#4019. 'Too Big A Risk' - Game Developer Sparks Debate After Delaying Playtest Due To AI Concerns

Will it push us towards a more cloud-focused future?

As AI continues to adopt a bigger influence in the gaming industry, there have been concerns in some circles about how people can use AI to reverse-engineer games, including for upcoming titles that haven't even been released yet.

This became a particular talking point a couple of weeks ago when Moonlighter developer Digital Sun Games decided to delay a planned (PC) playtest for their upcoming game ReVamp, worrying that the code might be reverse-engineered before they actually had a chance to release the full game.

Here's what they had to say in a statement at the time:

This ended up sparking a whole bunch of discussion regarding developers that might choose to adopt the same strategy, potentially opening us up to a future where demos and trials for upcoming games will become less prominent.

Some even took it further, suggesting that reverse-engineering will push us to a cloud-focused future:

A few people pushed back in the comments, suggesting that games have still been successful despite the existence of piracy and other elements that have threatened their potential over the years, while others highlighted that stronger protections in the future may be able to limit the damage from reverse-engineering situations.

For what it's worth, it's been reported in recent days that Claude has begun blocking attempts to clone and reverse-engineer games, and it was confirmed by an Anthropic dev that the idea is to "steer it away" from recreating other developers' titles because infringing IP is against the company's usage policy.

Ultimately though, it's too early to know what the future holds, but it's an interesting topic of discussion at the very least. Don't be surprised if instances like this still crop up, and hopefully it's something that Xbox is actively thinking about.

#4018. "Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale": Journey composer shares 20 minutes of music created during talks to work on BioWare's recently cancelled RPG

"It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever"

The gradual drip of details about and glimpses at what BioWare were looking to cook up with the cancelled Mass Effect 5 continues, this time thanks to a composer who was in talks to come aboard to put together the RPG's soundtrack. Said songsmith, Austin Wintory, has opted to share around 20 minutes of tunes he put together just as an attempt to explore where he might take things if he did end up being hired to score Commander Shepard's next adventure. Naturally, with BioWare's closure, that hasn't come to pass.

The eight tracks in the YouTube video Wintory, whose compositions have graced the likes of Journey and Assassin's Creed Syndicate, has put together range from a main theme, to intense battle tunes, and the sorts of 'ooh, there's something happening' songs that usually accompany key story moments. The opener, dubbed The Legacy of Shepard, blends pensive piano tinkling with bombastic sci-fi swells. The final track's a funkier remixed version of it. I think my favorite might be track seven, Forever Calibrating, just because it's the sort of relaxed and atmospheric backing tune I tend to put on for ambience while working.

"Working on Mass Effect 5 was my career's biggest dream project, my white whale," Wintory wrote in the video's description. "It is my favorite franchise of all time, and for the last couple years I'd been in serious conversations with BioWare and EA to jump in. My suggestion was to treat the original game's masterful Jack Wall/Sam Hulick score as a starting point, and to build on it from there with deeper use of physical, analog synths and a more tightly interwoven use of the orchestra. But a love letter first and foremost (not unlike my approach to the Aliens franchise with Fireteam Elite).

"As part of the ongoing dialogue, I decided last year (2025) to surprise the folks with an elaborate production: nearly 20 minutes of music, fully recorded and produced with synths, vocals and a large orchestra here in LA. I'd not yet learned any narrative details of what they were planning so this was just pure musical exploration. Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss. It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever."

The composer closed by thanking BioWare and EA's music department for giving him the chance to put together these experimental Mass Effect tracks.

While this outpouring of info about what BioWare were up to with Mass Effect 5 is likely all we'll ever get of it, given the folks who were working on it have been scattered to the winds, some fans of the series have begun petitioning for Shep's space adventures not to end up rotting in EA's big shed of disused game IP. Though, surprisingly, they appear not to be teaming that call with the assertion that it should ideally be the same devs who were working on the series prior to BioWare's closure that get first dibs on any opportunity to carry on making Mass Effects.

#4017. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 players are calling for a PvE-only version of its DMZ mode - just like every extraction shooter before it

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is officially out for all players, and its extraction shooter mode DMZ is looking to be particularly popular. And unsurprisingly, the mode's popularity has brought a longstanding player request back in the spotlight: many DMZ players have been asking developer Infinity Ward to provide a PvE-only variant of the extraction mode.

Curiously, the developer appeared to accidentally show a DMZ PvE option, which briefly got some players excited, only for Infinity Ward to later clarify it was actually a developer-only playlist, and that DMZ remains a purely PvPvE experience.

Now that millions have played it, however, it's become hard to browse the DMZ or Modern Warfare 4 subreddits without running into posts from players pleading with Infinity Ward to offer a playlist where they can play the mode without the presence of other humans.

"Please give players the option to play DMZ without PvP," one Reddit user wrote. "Losing your operator, weapons, equipment and collected loot because another squad ambushes you is incredibly frustrating. Having to pay upwards of 60,000 just to revive your operator, without recovering any lost gear, makes it even worse."

Although some have pushed back at the idea for seemingly invalidating the point of an extraction mode, others argue CoD: Warzone already does something similar. That mode, for instance, offers options to players who don't want to deal with a core aspect of battle royale, in letting them respawn after death. And so the argument goes that there's no reason why DMZ can't do the same.

"The common argument I see for NOT having a PvE only in DMZ is 'because that defeats the purpose of an extraction shooter.' Yet, Resurgence added respawns to the battle royale mode (Warzone)," argued another Reddit user. "The whole point of a battle royale is everyone for themselves, and you get ONE life."

A small number have even gone as far as to create an online petition, albeit to minimal success. One petition asking for a PvE mode has managed 331 signatures, at the time of writing.

It's also worth noting that Modern Warfare 4 doesn't offer any purely PvE modes beyond the campaign. Call of Duty players have come to expect at least one mode that's purely co-op and PvE in nature, such as Zombies, Spec Ops, or Endgame from last year's Black Ops 7. The push for a PvE version of DMZ is likely a factor of a contingent of players who feel the game is not catering to them the way it's typically done in recent years.

More broadly, of course, this phenomenon is not unique to DMZ; all popular extraction games have come to attract players who simply want to the looting, crafting, puzzle-solving and PvE combat without worrying about other players. Arc Raiders recently hosted a successful PvE playtest, and though it remains unclear whether the mode will return as a permanent addition, it was a major step for players who have been desperately asking for one since the game's launch.

Bungie's struggling Marathon has experimented with PvE modes, and now the studio is transforming the game to cater more to its Destiny audience, the majority of which want a PvE game. Meanwhile, the grandfather of the genre, Escape From Tarkov, held out long enough before eventually offering a PvE variant with its own progression in 2024.

That makes it seem almost inevitable that Infinity Ward would become subject to the same requests for DMZ. The catch is, as Arc Raiders and Tarkov have shown, these modes tend to take a long time to be implemented. The question then becomes whether or not that cohort of PvE-loving players will still be around once it arrives.

#4016. Stealth Classic Thief: The Dark Project Returns for a PS5 Remaster with New Content

One of the classics that helped create an entire genre, stealth masterpiece Thief: The Dark Project is coming to PS5 in remastered form next month, from 3rd December 2026.

This new version of the 1998 game has been remastered using Nightdive Studios' KEX Engine to produce a new edition running at 4K and 120 frames-per-second. It's got all the content of the base game, the three extra missions from Thief: Gold, and an entirely new campaign in the form of The Tarnished Mirror.

The Tarnished Mirror is a narrative bridge between The Dark Project and Thief 2: The Metal Age. In it, "a seemingly straightforward theft spirals into imprisonment, uneasy alliances and a descent into a drowned, R’lyeh-like necropolis. Players will experience an expanded enemy roster, ambitious level design and a pure Thief experience that descends into unsettling, otherworldly horror."

The bonus campaign has been created by the same people who made Thief: The Black Parade, which was a mod / expansion for Thief: Gold, made by the fans. "This collaboration marks a rare industry moment, with Nightdive and Eidos-Montréal welcoming a community creation directly into official canon," the press release added.

#4015. Steam Frame kernel updated with external CD-ROM drive compatibility just one day after a user asked Valve for it

Even with the importance of physical media ownership in the current era of digital product ephemera, it's often unlikely your PC will actually be able to play the CDs, DVDs or Blu-Rays you have around the house. Internal disc drives aren't common amongst desktops or even laptops anymore, so your only recourse is often an external drive.

One Steam Frame user was hoping to connect his own detachable disc drive to watch movies and play Need For Speed Carbon (valid!) using the headset, which can run both VR and 'flat' games without a separate PC, but found that the Frame lacked the drivers to read a disc. In a very earnest community post, user Aiodensghost lamented that this fact "KILLED MY ABILITY TO INSTALL MY ABANDONWARE FROM 2006. You don't sell NFS Carbon anymore (fuck you very much EA) [...] May I PLEASE have the ability to use an optical drive?" So polite!

A Valve employee by the username gaberowe would respond a day later, simply saying "we will look into this thanks for alerting us". Around ten minutes pass, and the 'deckard-linux-no-oopsies' GitHub repository (yes, it's really called that), which is the Linux kernel sources used in SteamOS for the Steam Frame, sees a commit from Rowe that effectively turns on CD-ROM support. More savvy Steam Frame users can hypothetically install the updated kernel themselves, as this commit enabled an existing Linux kernel feature, but it's likely that this support will simply be added in an upcoming software update.

In a news role where I am continually reporting on generative AI and layoffs, it's nice to report on something that boils down to 'software developer does something cool, quickly.' And, hey, Aiodensghost can play Need For Speed Carbon despite EA, which is always a gift.

#4014. Life is Strange makers Don't Nod face layoffs and possible insolvency, French workers union STJV state

Le Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo, a French game workers union, have released a statement detailing the current status of Don't Nod, the studio behind Life is Strange and Lost Records: Bloom and Rage. The studio's fate has been precarious for some time, but STJV now say that the studio has announced ("to financial press before the employees, as has been its MO") that it is under a "safeguard procedure" to avoid complete insolvency due to an inability to pay off its debts.

The studio's CEO, Oskar Guilbert, told employees that "a safeguarding process is an act of anticipation", in reference to the fact that last year, the CSE (employee representatives) were presented with two outcomes: either future games would find funding and staff would still be laid off, or no funding would be acquired, and the company would be liquidated. It seems the latter is now likely to come to pass, as STJV state that the company does not even have the funds to complete its pre-existing redundancies plan for laid-off employees. The union also note that "the CEO finished his address with empty remarks on how much attention was paid to employees, which everyone knows was bullshit and probably written by ChatGPT."

The statement goes on to clarify that the company will be unable to complete the last remaining project that was in development, referred to as P14. This is due to a huge incoming swathe of layoffs, which include "nearly all of the non-managerial jobs":

"6/6 animators, 3/3 character artists, 3/3 concept artists, 8/10 environmental artists, 2/3 sound designers, 4/8 game designers, 3/5 level designers, 6/6 associate producers, 18/22 programmers, 3/5 QA testers, 2/3 devops, 3/4 HR…

"Management is extremely clearly going for heavily individualized targeting and hasn’t been shy about their intent to keep selected people in rather than jobs, which is illegal."

In an apparent attempt to keep the studio running despite obliterating its staff, "management is betting its all on outsourcing", expecting managers to be able to keep things moving as normal despite the alleged shift to outsourcing and contractors taking on the existing work of fired staff. STJV put it better than I could: "Anyone with a little experience with video games production and sanity understands how out-of-touch such a plan is. The costs of outsourcing a project that was mostly internal up until now and the loss of the experience gained all throughout production seem to have been ignored in favour of short-term penny-pinching with unclear upsides."

The article closes by claiming that the CSE's negotiations with Don't Nod were essentially a farce, as the company had no intent of negotiating in the first place; "Management declares that it cannot offer anything: it’ll be the strict legal minimum and you’ll be glad for it." Concerns regarding the future of the studio have seemingly been made clear by the CSE for years, reportedly living with a sword of Damocles over their heads due to repeated mismanagement, miscommunication and gaslighting, but the future looks bleak. "They ignored the CSE, middle managers, the STJV, financial auditors, all because they believed unyieldingly that a miracle would come and they’d find funds for a game that was too big, too ambitious and ultimately too expensive."

The CSE consultation will reach its end on November 3rd, following which "the regional agency for employment and industry will have 21 days to decide on the plan, and if it is accepted, people could get their firing letters on November 25th." Though, if it is rejected, management would have to figure out a way forward other than insolvency, "because, as you might have gathered, planning for contingencies isn’t their forte."

#4012. Shenmue 3: Enhanced Edition has been delayed to "get everything right"

Grab your nearest forklift operator and make sure they're sitting down. Shenmue 3: Enhanced Edition has been delayed to 2027 in order to, as publisher Inin Games puts it, "get everything right".

"We're well aware that you're eagerly awaiting the chance to see Ryo shine like never before, for the first time on several modern consoles," Inin wrote in a newsletter update (thanks Shenmue Dojo). "Development is taking time to get everything right, and we’re making great progress while finalising the last details."

Shenmue 3: Enhanced Edition was originally expected to arrive in "Q4" this year, but Inin now says, "We'll have more details to share with you soon and are looking forward to this release in early 2027!" It'll be available on PC, PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2.

Shenmue 3: Enhanced Edition promises visual improvements to Ys Net's 2019 original, alongside quality-of-life changes, and performance boosts made possible by the modern hardware it'll be playable on. There's also talk of DLSS/FSR support, more NPC density within Niaowu, and a classic camera mode inspired by Shenmue and Shenmue 2.

The Enhanced Edition was first revealed in August 2025, and stands as a second shot for the divisive third entry in the legendary Dreamcast series. Despite its problems, , former Eurogamer editor-in-chief (and massive Shenmue fan) Martin Robinson still enjoyed Shenmue 3, describing it as "a bewitching time capsule that transports us to late 80s China, and to turn-of-the-century video games."

#4011. Two Big Remasters Are Now Lined Up For Xbox On December 3rd

Including a first-ever Xbox appearance for the original Thief!

It's usually the case that December is a quiet time for new video game releases, but we've still got a few notable ones lined up for the first couple of weeks on Xbox, including two very interesting remasters on December 3rd.

We already knew about the first of these - Rayman Legends Retold is coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S on that date. It seems a little bit redundant to "reimagine" an Xbox One game like Rayman Legends on the face of it, but the previews have been pretty great for the most part, and there's no doubt that Legends is a great game in general.

The next one has just been announced for December 3rd today though, and it's Thief: The Dark Project Remastered. The original Thief has never appeared on Xbox before, having first released on PC back in 1998, but it was considered one of the best games of that year across any platform, and has a whopping 92 average rating on Metacritic.

Its remaster is being handled by the experts at Nightdive Studios, known for an absolute ton of great remasters in recent years, so as long as you don't mind the dated nature of it, this could end up being a must-buy on the 3rd.

Exciting stuff! We'll leave you with more details on both games down below.

On this page: Two Big Remasters Are Now Lined Up For Xbox On December 3rd

Embark on a bold reimagining of the acclaimed platformer, filled with new content and narrative twists. When a shadowy villain spreads corruption across the Glade of Dreams, journey through its charming worlds solo or in up to 4‑player couch co‑op in a fast‑paced, side‑scrolling adventure where every stumble and surprise adds to the delightful chaos.

In Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, Nightdive Studios brings back the pioneering 3D stealth game from Looking Glass Studios. Described by its developers as a “first-person sneaker,” the 1998 title challenged norms with its non-confrontational gameplay at a time when most first-person games prioritized combat. Thief was the first stealth game to use light and sound as game mechanics to help you hide from and sneak up on characters, rather than simply attacking them. Remastered with Nightdive’s KEX Engine, the release includes Thief: The Dark Project and the additional missions, content and updates from the 1999 Thief Gold re-release.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is the talk of the town this week, not just because stock hunters are ready and waiting for its first special edition release but also while we count down the final days until its biggest release of the year so far.

Ocarina of Time remake is going to send everyone back to the '90s on November 5, but if you're not holding out for more Legend of Zelda Nintendo Switch 2 stock, Woot's getting upgraders there for $30 less this week. The Nintendo Switch 2 has dropped from $499 to $469 at the Amazon-owned retailer, but this one's going to move fast. I've previously only ever seen discounted refurbished units on these shelves and even they typically sell out before the day is done.

While we're still not at the $449 launch price of the handheld, Woot's $30 saving represents one of the first Nintendo Switch 2 deals to drop after the price increased in September.

Woot has sold Nintendo Switch 2 handhelds cheaper than this in the past, but rarely in new condition and this is the first time I've seen it here since the September 1 price increase.

Refurbished handhelds swallow up this shelf space every now and then, with the most recent offering landing back in October. Combining an on-screen discount with an additional discount tied to its gaming event, customers could grab renewed devices for as little as $409.

That was a perfect storm of savings we see typically once or twice a year. If you're upgrading your handheld ahead of Ocarina of Time (while still spending as little as possible), Woot's current Nintendo Switch deal will get you there for $50 less than the hard-to-find special edition release.

The discount is our GamesRadar+ Deal of the Day for November 2, but judging by the speed at which renewed offers have flown off the shelves at Woot it's not expected to last much longer. Unless you're holding out to roll the dice on Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals, time is of the essence here.

Unfortunately, there's a sad side to this story. While previously enjoying a $10 discount on physical pre-orders, both Amazon and Walmart have now run out of stock on the textured foil Ocarina of Time remake cart. If you want that physical case, you're now looking at the full $69.99 at Best Buy.

#4009. STALKER 2's latest update expands its A-Life NPC simulation bubble, seemingly without a scary performance tax

STALKER 2: Heart of Chornobyl has a new update out, 2.1, which builds on the excellent 2.0 patch by upgrading that most beloved and contentious of STALKER series features: the A-Life system that governs simulated NPC behavior. With the 2.1 update. It's now possible to whack up the distance at which A-Life NPCs (who, unlike scripted characters, will wander around, fight others over faction turf, and sometimes hunker down for a campfire-side guitar sesh) are visualised, while audio tweaks can make these unplanned shootouts audible from further away. The effect, in theory, is a better sense of the Zone's inhabitants going about their bang-banging business, even if Mr. Main Character here isn't close by.

Both the updated game and the accompanying blog post warn that cranking this A-Life bubble up beyond the lowest, default 'Recommended' setting may have adverse effects, ranging from lower framerates to "story quest instability" and crashes. Fearing a return to STALKER 2's bug-ridden early days, I tried out the new A-Life distance options on the RPS test rig, and found they're not actually that perilous – though they might do strange things with binoculars.

To judge the performance effect, I ran the rig's RTX 4060 at 1080p, with Quality-level DLSS and the High preset - save for having the draw distance setting on Epic, to maximise the potential visualisation. Walking through an open, A-Life-ripe patch of the Zone produced a 93fps average on Recommended, which remained unchanged on the Extended setting, before barely dropping to 91fps on the Highly Extended, Maximum and Dynamic settings. Well that's not so bad! The warnings made it sound like the bigger options would ignite the air around my graphics card and brainwarp quest NPCs into thinking they were in Barbie Horse Ride & Rescue (available now on Steam). 2fps? That's nothing. Nothing.

Granted, results may vary depending on your PC specs; the RTX 4060 isn't especially potent but it was backed up by a good CPU and a healthy 32GB of RAM, which likely helped handle the extra computations required for a wider sprawl of distant gunfights. To get a fuller picture, I did try a different approach, leaving ground level to claim a lofty concrete vantage point and- god dammit, recently added fog effects.

Still, the Zone's unknowable RNG calculations were not kind, and after several minutes of fruitless waiting I returned to run more tests on terra firma.

I ultimately didn't find anything else that would suggest an unacceptable risk of performance loss or instability, though I did discover one quirk of the new system: in addition to render distance, your choice of A-Life setting also appears to influence the range at which faction markers show up on binoculars.

More strangely, selecting Maximum A-Life also seems to… increase the zoom of binoculars? As you can see in those two shots, which were snapped from the same position. I guess it's a bug but hey, if GSC are telling me I can get better NPC simulation and a magnification upgrade for the low, low price of two frames per second, I'll take that deal.

STALKER 2 2.1 is out now for everyone. Besides the A-Life distance gubbins, it also adds the ability to tag along with roaming fellow stalkers, turning them into mobile fast travel stations - though, in keeping with the notion that NPCs don't actually give a toss about you, they'll only warp you to places that their specific patrol route was passing anyway.

Asked if there's anything being planned for the occasion, Suda51 says his team and publisher Marvelous are indeed cooking up something. (Quotations machine translated.)
